The sun beats down as the galleon plods rhythmically through the gentle open ocean. An alarm cry from the crows nest. The quiet sea begins to boil as the terrible mecha phoenix of the Enemy rises from the water and into the sky. Cries of terror and resignation as the creature bursts aflame and slams its wings into the hull in a furious rage, capsizing and igniting the vessel as the horribly blackened crew all sink lifelessly to their demise.
Show-opening version makes the 2023 "Rockdale" double-time pivot and hits a series of great peaks before returning home. The beginning of the song's jamming resurgence.

jamchart_note: Another masterclass in drums and percussion drive the majority of this jam. Last few minutes highlighted by Peter's haunting keys as guitar/synth effects and bass provide the perfect backdrop.

footnote: With Arkansas Traveler teases from Rick and Peter.

jamchart_note: For the Bird’s first big amphitheater outing, “November Rain” and “Layla” codas hatch a tiny chick and implant it deep within your amygdala, pecking squarely at your heartstrings in a crescendoing symphony. Paralyzed by pangful euphoric blinding rapture, the soul inflates as a metaphysical supernova, slowly bursting through… departing… leaving vacancy in your Earthly shell for the Wolf to take hold.

show_notes: This show was part of the Resonance Music & Arts Festival. I'm Alright and Make the Move were played for the first time since August 23, 2022 (74 shows).

jamchart_note: This single-jam version moves into a bouncy danceable space that feels like something that might evolve from a second jam. Probably organic but possibly an intentional nod to the historical focus on electronic music at Resonance.

footnote: With Lily's Tiger tease from Peter.

jamchart_note: Peter goes crazy on this "Arrow": synthy dreaminess, marimba dance style jamming, helicopter and alarm horn background effects, subtle voice drops (woo’s?), double guitar darkness. Once he shifts back to melodic keys you know final drive to peak is coming (and it delivers!).
Typical mellow start until Ben begins tribal drumming, Rick changes to a grungier tone and jam thrusts into a nasty rock build.

show_notes: This show was part of the Resonance Music & Arts Festival. Dancing in the Moonlight was played for the first time since March 3, 2022 (112 shows).

jamchart_note: Extra raunchy clav by Peter kicks off before the switch to piano gives Rick the space to start laying the foundation for what becomes a frantic journey through a sonic maze. The 13 minute mark begins the fast tempo escape from the morass. Soaring guitar work by Rick builds the jam to a couple really nice peaks before reentry.

The Umphress Of Organos (Umphrey’s McGee sit-in): after the typical beautiful Trevor solo, Joel Cummins & Pete trade off on keys wonderfully then hand over to Jake Cinninger & Rick for a diabolical, multi-part shredfest.
footnote: With Jake Cinninger on guitar and Joel Cummins on keys.

show_notes: Wild Night was played for the first time since October 6, 2022 (67 shows). During Creatures and Arcadia, Fourth of July fireworks were set off on the boardwalk.

footnote: 80s synth version. With Welcome to Delta jam.

jamchart_note: Rick hits a repeating pattern that band lock on around, Pete beautifully hits a perfectly timed synth and then jam energetically takes off in best version to date. Rick is an absolute rock god in this absurdly beautiful finish.
Groove locks in and departs "Yeti" proper before one of the band's best segues to date into "Creatures."

Perfect segue out of "Yeti" and it's all gravy from there. Energy on top of energy on top of energy for 20 minutes while fireworks begin going off in the background. The following "Arcadia" finishes out a wild trio to celebrate the 4th on the boardwalk.
Not an atypical version musically or very long, but the 4th of July fireworks and INSANE energy make this one special.
Pete given a mid-jam opportunity to shine on the keys and after a quick solo, creates a salsa-like groove that band picks up on. First version to have the fast, “happy” "Dripfield" ending.

show_notes: What's Up was played for the first time since October 7, 2022 (67 shows).

jamchart_note: Trevor driving as he often does with "Thatch," but this time with simple-yet-cool riffs and melodies that the band latches onto and then builds around. Stank face inducing rock in the last 6 minutes.
footnote: With Secret Agent Man tease from Peter.

jamchart_note: Foregoing the initial rocking section and peak we’ve seen in many 2023 versions, the band immediately settles for a quieter, gentler jam. Results in Rick finding a pretty riff with around 5 mins to go that everyone hooks onto and builds into a really pretty glory peak.

Goose begins taking a gentler approach than the usual Hot Tea and finds a gorgeous pocket of melodic bliss and patiently and beautifully builds around it. Heart-warming, smile-inducing joy in a way that very few bands can induce.
Very Floyd-like section gives a really psychedelic vibe to the first half of this version.

show_notes: This was Goose's biggest headlining show to date.

jamchart_note: Kicking off a stretch of great jamming in their first visit to SPAC, starts with lovely Pete and Rick solos & then confidently packs an extra punch, taking the jam on one of its longest rides and leading to a gorgeous, energetic final 4 minutes (capped by Trevor Bass).

Extended, spicy Trevor and Peter solos to start the jam as crowd energy comes through the recording. Rick comes in hot for a minute but band decides to shift and explore. Dynamic, energetic rocking continues to build in intensity until darker chaos takes over, finally releasing into joyous finish. Will take set opener Empress any day!

Jam quickly mellows out into a quiet-yet-tight groove. "Tequila" teasing adds some flavour as the band gradually increases the energy and explodes. Amazing mid-set version from the legendary SPAC debut.

Tribal, triumphant set 2 closer of an epic show. Sit back and enjoy Ben and Jeff put on a percussive masterclass while synths swirl and Rick brings down the house with a thrashing, thunderous finish. "Happy" Dripfield ending and synths continue while band walks off stage.

Fitting encore for their largest show to date, band almost stops playing after final verse and toys with spacey effects before epic build up into passionate, conquering jam full of swagger. Return to fast, melodic style as the band seems intent to burning the venue to the ground in their final moments on stage.

footnote: Blind Melon. With Magic School Bus theme tease from Rick and Peter.

jamchart_note: Fall tour opens with a blazing hot "Drive" that sees the band stretch out the solo section into some great dual-guitar madness.
show_notes: (dawn) was played separately from SOS for the first time since January 26, 2022 (136 shows).

jamchart_note: "Flee" had a pretty good Fall and it all started here. Right when the rocking jam is about to wrap up with the closing guitar solo, this unfinished version instead veers into a delightfully whimsical little passage akin to early 90's Frisell interpreting ragtime music. Peter moves from vibes to clav in a satisfying fashion during a slick transition into "Look Out Cleveland".
Synthy, psychedelic vibe largely thanks to Spuds' pounding toms and Peter's delayed Vintage Vibe work. Really incredible use of keyboard effects.

This Boston run was Vintage Vibe heaven. Peter lays it on THICK, infusing vibrato and distortion into the heavy chords in the early dark segment as Rick shreds alongside. Makes a bright shift and soars through a series of glorious peaks before returning home.

Second big Boston "E or A?" of 2023. Jam begins to break into space with some octave-up from rick and reverb-drenched marimba from Peter, though still anchored in the song's progression. Second half hits double-time and explodes outward into a sunny afternoon of a peak. Just nonstop momentum.

Dark and synthy. Learning lessons from each version on the road to Boston, this one has some amazing eerie texturing from Peter, while Rick and Trevor growl in the darkness. Gradually picks up steam with the same ominous Prophet synth undertone throughout. Excellent display of tension-building here.

An important stop on the journey to the insanity at Red Rocks in just a few weeks, we are treated to another dive into Vintage Vibe darkness as the rhythm section holds down a beautiful bedrock for Rick and Peter to weave around each other. Run through a brick wall with the momentum of this one.

show_notes: This show was part of the Borderland Music + Arts Festival.

jamchart_note: Featuring Taylor and Griffin of Dawes. Huge version has some great guitar interplay in the first half before setting into glorious bliss land for the second half. Jeff loves that D chord!
footnote: With Taylor Goldsmith on guitar and vocals, Griffin Goldsmith on drums, and Jeff on guitar.

jamchart_note: Initial two-guitar duelling fragments into marimba space and slows down into some classic Fall '23 bliss-building. Hints of the reverse "Heartbreaker" riff Rick loves so much punch through at the peak before Peter leads into a piano-centric outro jam that might just be the best part of the whole thing.

Elizabliss chugs right into a gorgeous, intoxicating bliss jam that smoothly builds and builds to a triumphant peak, with Rick’s guitar tone sparkling like the Champagne of beers in the Miller High Life Theatre.

footnote: Slow, melodic version. With Secret Agent Man tease from Rick and Peter and Long Tall Glasses tease from Rick.

jamchart_note: -> in from "Myst." Picks up where the groove left off and builds up a powerful head of steam before heading smoothly into "Take On Me," finishing out an excellent trio of songs to begin the second set.

jamchart_note: Never really departs the Delta space but has some excellent Peter exploration of tones on clav and Vintage Vibe. A fun listen.

jamchart_note: Spacey and textural with hints of "Dragonfly." Gets funkier out of the murk with a laid-back vibe and hits a series of bluesy rock peaks almost like the 10/4/22 "This Old Sea."

show_notes: The Killing Moon was played for the first time since November 7, 2020 (190 shows). Moby was played for the first time since January 15, 2023 (55 shows).

jamchart_note: Spuds quickly turns percussive as Peter hits repeating patterns on the Vibe. Fragments into the Eastern-tinged space they love so much with circular riffs from Rick and Peter that give it a very dissonant and darker feel.

A rare fully-two-guitar jam for 2023. Deconstructs into a seriously groovy interplay section driven by Spuds' clap stack. Still pretty much Type I throughout but a very fun and groovy listen. Peter hits the keys right at the end with hints of Ted Tapes riffing as they > to an explosive "Red Bird."

Whether you think it's the JOTY or not, this "Thatch" is a seriously dense listen. Dark and percussive at first, it feels very typical for the tour but quickly heads into evil territory thanks to Rick and Peter's interplay. Spuds pivots into a charging beat at the 18th minute and they just go for it. Superlatives can't even do this peak justice - needs to be listened. Rick plays with his Whammy at the apex before they execute a perfect and towering return to the song proper. All-timer.
Very "In Your Eyes"-tinged jam. Upbeat and feel-good, this version signifies that Goose is finally finding their footing with big "Dripfield" jams and breaking the mold.

footnote: With River Lullaby tease from Rick.

show_notes: This was Jeff's 200th show in the band.

"Spokane Word" Original Trevor Weekz poetry, an amalgamation.

jamchart_note: Standard fare until the last five minutes or so, when the band breaks into some terrifyingly evil improv. Layers of dark textures thanks to Peter's synths and clav while Rick opts for some more laid-back riffing. One of the best segments of the tour.

jamchart_note: The third festival "Kylie" of the year breaks from form in an amazing "Elmeg the Wise"-like jam. Triumph.
Eschews the usual blistering and fast-paced jam in favour of a laid-back and major-key space. Shorter version that will draw you in for repeated listens.

Peppy jam begins with Spuds on punchy tom work as Peter lays into the Vibe. Turns spacey and then falls away into a bouncy funk jam that feels totally unique to Goose's sound. Trevor and Rick lock in on some riffs while Peter moves to a textural role throughout the contemplative and unhurried groove. Must-listen to understand the developmental period of Fall '23.

show_notes: Nights In White Satin was played for the first time since October 14, 2022 (77 shows).

jamchart_note: Another stellar outing for the song in '23, this Liz finds herself ever-so-gently tugging at threads of the bay area "Dark Star" concentrate in the fabric, pulling Inspiration from the cosmos for the truly gorgeous bliss jam to come.

Not your average set-closing rocker. The band moves beyond standard Peter shred territory to an all-out party jam with a euphoric feel. Foot on the gas, it peaks for several minutes straight before sliding back into the song proper.

Second big "Drip" of fall tour breaks form into the familiar percussive play with Rick and Peter dancing around each other. Sticks in this zone for a while until a shift into an amazing and expressive bliss-rock peak. Beautiful stuff.

This fluid and vibrant Flee is at its best during the masterful emotive solo Rick guides the first half of the jam with, Peter dancing along with every note in some of his very finest piano accompaniment.

jamchart_note: Choogles along as normal until the 11th minute, when Peter and Trevor lock in on a major-key transition. Rick flips on the octave-up overtop a low synth drone as Goose takes it really slow and patient in a build that reminds some of "Pancakes" or "Wolfman's Brother." Whatever you want to call it, it's absolutely phenomenal. Special highlight to the gong TEXTURES that Jeff lays down.
Peter hits the Vibe early on in the jam as the pace is set. Fun "Magic School Bus" teases pivot into a great peak section that make this the standout OG "AIN" since 2019.

jamchart_note: First jammed version of "Sea" in 2023 gets bluesy and rocking. Rick toys with a riff similar to Zeppelin's "Moby Dick" as Peter whales on the organ. Guitar takes over as the band hits a feel-good peak and just sustains it for a long time.

Newly rearranged "EMG" jam segment is perfectly suited to the pure evil that develops at Red Rocks. Locking in on a theme like the hallowed 1/30/22 "Wysteria" and 6/10/22 "AIN," Rick just doesn't let up for a second as Spuds and Jebb go wild on the primal drums. Trevor drops massive bombs as Peter hammers piano chords and the darkness just BUILDS. Absolutely astounding improv.
Closes the first set like its recent counterpart in Oakland. Gets outside of standard "Yeti" for some fun peak jamming.
Continuation of the mellower and more upbeat "Thatch" style seen at the Wiltern on 9/28. Rocking first half transitions into a quieter space that builds into an excellent peak.

This top shelf "Factory Fiction" jam begins with a snarling slow burn. Eventually finding its way into a patiently developed anthemic Rick-led "Dragonfly" jam, this sonic assault on the alien landscape of Red Rocks concludes in an explosive fashion that merits repeat listens.

jamchart_note: Second song ever played in Europe goes full bliss rock mode. Soaring first jam, crunchy middle segment, and then another excellent peak to close.

Peter runs marimba through the Leslie for a haunting and unique effect early on. Rick and Trevor lock in on some melodies as the effects continue to dominate. The band emerges as Spuds picks up the pace and seems to be heading for bliss land, but Peter delays that shift with layers and layers of reverbed piano. Eventually hits a blistering peak and returns home.

jamchart_note: Trevor and Peter find a really catchy repeating downward progression theme that the band builds around. Excellent gradual collective cool down that allows band to side into "Borne."

Surprise jam out of this cover gets dark and nasty with layered Leslie marimba and organ from Peter while Spuds absolutely punishes his kit. Can't tell if it's the band or crowd screaming here either!

Highlight of the Jamsterdam show, Peter shines as he drives mood of jam with simple yet powerful selections on keys throughout, ending in beautiful Blissteria collective band magic. Slides into a really great "Electric Avenue."
Eugene "Borne"-style jamming for the middle few minutes as the band gets atypically quiet and patient. Layers of textures are absolutely breathtaking and it's a shame it's so short!
Peter collects a bunch of coins early on as the rhythm section destroys the minimalist funk groove. Rick pivots into triumph and the band unleashes a volcanic peak to close it out.
Gorgeous bliss finish.

Longest "Lee" to date doesn't go too far from home, at least initially, as Peter dials up some synth undertones. Hits on some "Dragonfly" elements before Spuds takes control as he was wont to do on the Europe '23 tour. Peter plays with motif's almost like Vulfpeck's "Tee Time" as Rick shreds up to the finish.

jamchart_note: Free-flowing, collective no-one-take-the-lead improv as you can find little moments throughout where any 2 band members riff of each other only to have the others join in. Gradual, patient build leading to explosive peak.

Quickly heads for Winter 2022-style dark jamming. Trevor gets DEEP into Spuds' pocket as Rick's angular soloing swirls around Peter's eerie piano. Synths come in as it gets heavier and into some carnival-like zones before the band bails back into the "Echo" ending.

footnote: With Within You Without You tease from Peter.

jamchart_note: Immediately dropping into a darker key akin to the Red Rocks version, this jam pulsates and is driven forward by ferocious drumming, slowly building to majestic glorious rock.

footnote: Prince. With Axel F teases from Rick.

jamchart_note: After funky start where Luigi finds his coins, Peter layers mystical synths and Rick finds a haunting repeating riff that propels a wonderfully unique and enchanting version. Thrilling finish.

Blistering Type I play cools into a brief "Shama" fakeout before Goose unleashes one of the best bliss jams in recent memory. Calling to mind the Cap "Drive," each member takes their time with the theme and delivers an absolutely incredible peak.

After Peter tells crowd they have one more song, Rick rips back into a second Drive jam to end the show. A fiery theme develops and eventually morphs into the "(dawn)" finish. Incredible spontaneous moment.

Some nasty Type I churn explodes through the first part of the jam but cools around 13:30. Peter's staccato repeated riff informs the next part of the jam, where the band plays with a theme akin to the ending of "Dripfield." Great upbeat groove modes.

Summoning the ghost of the ‘21 Legend Valley "Madhuvan," this sub-14-minute version contains an incredible stop/start jam, alternating back and forth between peaceful serenity and possessed heavy metal shredding.

Rick finds a melody that he likes and Goose shreds to a peak of epic proportions. Final night of tour throw-down.

jamchart_note: “DDS”/“The Doctor Will See You Now” vocal shenanigans lead to gorgeous bliss. Ben eventually hits double time and jam builds to soaring, beautiful first climax. Just when you think it may be winding down in minute 21, band rips back in and explodes the finish. One of the best jams, if not the best, of Euro Tour 23.

jamchart_note: Not your average "strap in" CCR cover. Peter hits the Vibe as the jam begins and the band embarks on a wildly spacey Type II journey that eventually winds around to the conclusion of "Echo of a Rose." Look for this song again in 2024.

jamchart_note: A fitting conclusion to the tenth Goosemas that also was Spuds' final song - though we didn't know at the time. Nothing out of the ordinary but a special, fiery "Arcadia" that takes some extra spins around the ending as the band took a moment to relish their Hampton accomplishment.

jamchart_note: Cotter's first big jam and the band does not hold back one iota. First developing a ripping dual-guitar jam for several minutes - very active Trevor - before Cotter seamlessly transitions into the "second jam." Patiently builds into a bliss motif reminiscent of the ending of "SOS," peaking massively and concluding just short of the 31-minute mark.

jamchart_note: Not multi-section like the first set's "Drive" but is at least as good. Chaos slowly begins to creep in as Rick introduces a dark melody to build upon as Cotter really shows what he can do. Perfect re-entry atop the peak as Rick gradually teases the ending "Pancakes" riff a number of times before committing to the landing. Must-hear.

Revised arrangement with propulsive drumming from Cotter leads to a jam that could not be more different from Fall '23 versions. Initially winds up in a great blissy space that reaches a natural conclusion, but the band instead opts to put the pedal to the metal and strike into a dance groove. Peter hits into some filthy envelope filter clav work before transitioning into marimba while Rick slowly guides the band back into the euphoric conclusion of the song.
First version with Jeff on acoustic guitar and it sounds great. Jam coalesces into a cool groove before sliding perfectly -> to "Factory Fiction," probably the most notable thing about this one.

show_notes: This show was on the day of a total solar eclipse and featured a full performance of Moon Cabin.

jamchart_note: After an energetic and extended jam, Goose begins to slowly morph into one of the most feel good, happy, grin-inducing jams they've ever played. A jam so happy, it’s like watching the entirety of Ted Lasso season one in 30 seconds.

footnote: With Luigi's Raceway tease from Peter.

jamchart_note: A breathtaking and beautiful take on the song. Doesn't stray far from "Rosewood" proper but showcases remarkable patience as the band builds together to a dreamlike peak. Rick throws in some excellent dark tension-building moments toward the end as well.

Great dual-guitar churn on the front end, but the last few minutes of deconstructive and contemplative play are the real star. Showed potential for further exploration but was abandoned in favour of a concise "Echo of a Rose."
show_notes: It Burns Within was played for the first time since March 12, 2023 (79 shows).

jamchart_note: Dark and propulsive jam led by Peter on the OB-6. Not the deepest improvisationally but an excellent listen.

The band spends the first minutes after the vocal rounds poking at the edges of the melody until finally casting the bit. Then it's drill, baby, drill. The jam loops, but with purpose. It takes a pointed journey, uncovering new layers as it spirals deeper into the core of its oblique melody, creating an ever-changing tapestry of sound. Cotter energetically closes his first "Bird" with rolling tom work over creative breakbeats while Rich toys with an almost Middle Eastern "Minarets"-style riff.

Jam begins from nothing as Rick begins to build a sinister motif. Peter lays down delayed Vibe as the rest of the band enters and gradually build into a beautifully evil churn. Rick then signals to Cotter at the apex and the drums drive forward into double-time, bringing us home in a blaze of glory to bookend this second set. Some really wild and articulate heavy metal builds from Rick.
First jammed version since 10/6/22 gets into an airy space quickly with Rick sticking to form at first.

Peter goes full Cory Wong mode on the initial jam segment as he takes a stroll around the stage. Eschewing the typical B-flat modulation to go into jam territory, the band fragments out of the funk and quickly builds into gorgeous major-key play led by Vintage Vibe and Rick's emotional soloing. jamchart_note: It's your classic festival set "Myst" -> "Kylie"...until it's not. Amazing textures in a synth-drenched wind-down on the outro.

A sludgy and mysterious exit from the song structure leads to some typical jamming that progressively gets more melodic over the course of 12 minutes or so until Rick latches onto the theme that becomes the centerpiece. He deftly builds up to the peak backed by Cotter’s staccato attack for 5 minutes of triumphant glory. We don’t know what we’ve won, but we’re certain we’re victorious.

Cotter's first "AIN" opens summer tour on a strong note. Gets into some percussive space before a brief major section gives way to a spacier and dark-tinged mode. Peter goes to guitar for the last few minutes as they explore some new territory before sliding perfectly -> to "Flee."

Initial standard "Borne" jamming gets into some weird territory just before the 20-minute mark thanks to Cotter and Trevor. Envelope filter bass gets augmented by choppy clav from Peter as Rick lays down loops, eventually smoothly morphing into an upbeat and rocking peak. Hell of an omen for the rest of tour.

Rick's new synth pedal gets a workout as the band plays the first of many amazing versions of "Empress" in summer '24. Late-night disco groove emerges, which will be a prevalent theme throughout the tour.

The band departs from initial funk together in a rocking progression with Peter laying down chunky guitar behind Rick's soloing. Downshifts with a major modulation and follows a familiar uplifting pattern as Cotter pushes the tempo. Hits a strong peak before returning to funk and hints at "Arrow" ahead of the song's conclusion.

Circular patterns of tension and darkness develop as Cotter's fluidity shines. Builds layers and layers of unease as Peter hits sirens and Rick gets dissonant. Amazing stuff that can be likened to a mid-90s "Stash."

Roaring down the open road, radio blaring “...and the road goes on forever I’ve got one more silver...”, feeling mellow mischievous, the sea pans into view. Now barreling along the cliffs the Rider abruptly plunges into the sea, radio cut dead in the depths replaced by embryonic deep whooshing saline heartbeat. Feeling a needful pull toward the surface a triumphant new driving rhythm crackles the airwaves while screaming ablaze toward shouts emanating from vermin in their wooden coffin soon-to-be a pyre.
Blasts out of an excellent "Red Bird" into a blistering hot jam.

The Taco Town of “Empresses.” We start with the top slice: an unprecedented six-minute pre-verse intro jam. Then, savor the thick, crunchy layer after Trevor’s bass solo. You think you’ve reached the meat, but then you’re swept into a “River” of “Greens.” Think we’re done? Not quite. The real core of this sandwich is the bottom half, with “Empress” returning for a jam-packed, savory finish that ties it all together.

The bottom half of the "Empress" sandwich starts with the same layer that topped the "Green River" center. The band settles into a steady, chill groove, with Rick’s digital sauce poured over Pete’s thick layer of vintage vibes. This section is light but thick, a monolith revealing a slightly spicy aftertaste before dissolving into brief almost "Flowdown"-like dissonance. A final dark spread evocative of Mario’s underworld theme, coats the bottom slice’s closing verses and composed finish.

Seventeen months younger and still cutting his teeth, Eugene's baby brother enchants the neighboring northwest with a worthy, if less mature, reprise. Built on a bed of vintage vibes and a steady, pulsing bassline, the performance explores a richly textured, atmospheric space as Rick patiently vamps until finding a hook around the 14-minute mark. For the last few minutes, the band shifts to a dancier chordal groove that never fully realizes its potential, dissolving instead into "Turned Clouds."

Another great S1 closer that starts forebodingly with some minor key piano and is driven forward by tribalistic drumming. After a little tension, Rick settles back gently and melodically before band patiently and collectively builds up to EMG’s typical ripping conclusion. Cotter truly shines throughout

Grungy double guitar rock and roll takes a magical tour through blisstown. Gorgeous melodic finish before slipping into "Electric Avenue." Very reminiscent of the SPAC version from earlier in the month.

Machine gun fire drowns out the engines roar as the vehicle veers off the road in a raging inferno. Speed up. Target marked. Repeat. Targets in the rear view spin out in perfectly timed oil slicks. Patterns repeat mechanically as the G-6155 races, explosions mirroring the pits of our drivers eyes. A boat house looms on the horizon as a helicopter blasts impassable craters in the road ahead. Now airborne our driver ignites and spins skyward shrieking as whirling blades & debris plummet toward scorched earth.

Ecstasy. Infectious optimism. Pure Joy. Rick finds a repeating hook at 7:45 that he builds around before an explosion of guitar Rock Goddery. Every time you think he's found the apex of energy within the peak, he unlocks a new level of earworm shredding. He then slows down, brilliantly going back into the earlier riff before deciding to hose down the crowd one last time. This song DELIVERS as a set closer.
Great section later in the jam akin to the Westville "Rockdale," a demented and askew motif thanks to Cotter's urging.
Some heavier riffing in the latter half of the jam makes this version stand out from the 2024 pack.

Equal parts vibesy vibes, angular reverse delay, Big T fulcrum lines, cyclonic tribal toms, digital sauce, and staccato guitar attack, all culminating in a plucked-from-thin-air melody for Rick's closing solo, permuted several times before dissolving into the composed ending. Sultrily stirred.

jamchart_note: Spaces out from the initial funk with Peter laying down thick guitar chords. Two-guitar Goose reflects the first light of sunrise, its shamanic texture a tribute to the crisp dawn. The band patiently floats in that space before shifting into a frenetic and exploratory Ted-like jam. Returning to the song structure, Pete transitions to punctuated keys, inviting Rick into a cyclical step-jam typical of “Madhuvans.” With callbacks to the earlier “Mais Que Nada,” Rick builds to a deliberate peak, both provoked and matched by Trevor’s fierce, Cliff Burton-like bassline.

First significant Boat in a LONG time goes AGGRESSIVE funk. Rick alternates between sharp MuTron and distorted leads while Peter sets up a slick arpeggiator. Bingo “FITS” finally meets its match, stepping into the ring like Tyson facing Paul. The lockdown-tested heavyweight takes on Cincy’s arpeggiated, perennially online underdog — brimming with digital flair, youthful creativity, nimble footwork, and fog machine bravado. It’s a decision by points, with this scrappy “Fish” revealing new motifs, layers, sounds and overall vibes for one of the best covers in the catalogue.

jamchart_note: At a svelte 15 minutes, one of the year’s most satisfying and efficient performances. Out of the verses, it drops immediately into a patient half-time jam undergirded by sultry organ and Big T funk. Channeling David Gilmour, Rick fills space with the fewest possible notes, crafting an ethereal soundscape. Lead guitar takes to the fore with a bluesy jam that dissolves into a brief Rush-like prog passage before building to a satisfying tension-and-release peak.

A bonded pair of Entities strafe over the abandoned capital city raining molten cataclysmic destruction and salted earth. Time skipping through the ether bubble we emerge underground to witness VOID then the faint glow of long-dead embers reignited in a haunting pulse of malevolent shades of red and sparkling whites. Coalescing to crystalline form the patterns blink in ancient code as structure takes form stretching outward sprouting into a vast shallow sea of shimmering fractalien beauty. Life finds a way.
Pivots out of funk into excellent full-band bliss.

jamchart_note: The late-blooming younger brother of 24's monstrous high-school quarterback and homecoming king, "Cap Drive." The sibling resemblance is unmistabkle, with the same prominent good looks and form. But while 24's two-guitar Goose section immediately unleashes a colossal wall of sound, this one ambles through the halls of adolescent uncertainty before finally finding its senior-year stride — ignited by Rick’s delicate yet forceful guitar-work, Pete’s sudden organ attack, and Cotter’s thunderous drumming.

jamchart_note: The most remarkable thing about this “Animal” is how unexpectedly non-"Animal" it reads. A listener jumping in blindly right after the verses could easily get lost in the sauce of a typical “Arcadia” jam. We find Ricky doing that trademark Ricky thing, with a gradual sustained build patiently transforming a simple musical idea into a high-energy, major-key bliss explosion. This rendition portends of only good things for “Animal," quite possibly as the next big jam vehicle.

Most exploratory version to date hangs in some low-key funk out of the gate. First of two behemoth versions from Winter '25. Two-guitar Goose at its FINEST. Rick and Peter get scratchy as Trevor leads Cotter into a heavy and dark space. From there, it's all-out pandemonium as the band moves from one menacing idea to the next, shifting and evolving through tones as the tension just builds and builds. Explodes into a peaky section as Cotter RELENTLESSLY pushes the pace through the finish.
First show-opening version ever sets the tone for an incredible night with an efficient and well-paced peak jam.

Massive first-set version heads from usual minor-key space into some classic Winter '25 musings, opening way up with dark Rick and Peter. Hits an early peak in a vicious mode before Cotter picks up the pace and things get intensely psychedelic. Reverb clav twines with guitar melodies as the two find a new tension-filled riff and let it simmer and boil before things hit a final wave of tension into the cathartic "EMG" ending. Your jaw will be on the floor. Winner of JOTY 2025.

Celebratory, uplifting, and charging as the band coalesces around a single idea and rips through it in a way that will have you punching the roof of your car in excitement. Phenomenal set-closing peak in an absolutely incredible show that fades out unfinished.

An immediate GOAT contender, this longest-to-date “FITS” sits shoulder to shoulder with Bingo and Taboose versions. The conventional arpeggiated theme and rock-anthem guitar hero riff are swiftly eschewed in favor of a re-sequenced “Stranger Things”-inspired synth line. Pete layers commanding piano and evocative vibes to create a lush sonic bed over which Rick unleashes an expansive solo evoking 90s-era Santana.

First version to break free of its boundaries carries the energy of the surprise jammed-out "FITS" that came right before. Upbeat, rocking, and celebratory, the band never strays too far into the unknown but keeps up some amazing energy throughout before winding its way home. Possibly an indication that there are plans for bigger excursions in the future...

jamchart_note: Breaking the longest stretch on the bench since its debut, this "Flee" departs standard play quickly thanks to Rick diving into loops. Creating a hypnotic atmosphere in tandem with the repeating sounds, Peter lays down some piano riffs as we stretch out. Cotter lays in some excellent cymbal washes before upping the tempo and energy while Rick takes us through a seriously blistering peak. Fades atop the toms and slides -> into "Atlas Dogs."

Pleasant major-key space evolves quickly with Rick on some very purposeful melodic leads overtop Peter's synth drone. Cools from there as the band finds a darker progression, Rick augments his tone, and we're off to the races. Some serious Rick fireworks as the energy ramps up, matched beautifully by Peter's repetitive piano work. Boils into a wild tension-build before coming home strong.

Calls back to the 12/13/24 "Hungersite" in the way that Peter builds a repetitive soaring riff on clav for the first part. The band hits a beautiful peak before cooling into a minute of moody play akin to Ted Tapes cut "Arrokoth" before moving on to "Interlude II."
Major key post-rock progressions into blistering crescendos? Sign us up for MORE. OF. THIS. PLEASE. Absolutely crushed this hallowed cover, making it their own in yet another whole new way.

jamchart_note: Even the Benatar cover received a little extra mustard on this night. Peter lays down a bed of synth effects and bouyant vintage vibes for Rick to emote over, delivering a slowly woven lyrical crescendo thematically akin to the Schuyler Sisters theme in Hamilton, notably showcased in "Satisfied".

Some of the best amorphous jamming yet. Fans of the Eugene "Borne" will enjoy this next phase in the evolution of the ambience/texture over melody/structure model. Peter's inpsirational synth work melds with full band to evoke the serene feeling of ice floes in the arctic gently undulating in the waves under the aurora borealis, while a pod of whales calls to the heavens. Rick tugs the OIOO theme back in over this 90's new age excursion in a truly stunning fashion, not a dry eye in the house, into "Animal".

First version to ever open a second set and it's immediately right at home. Absolute two-guitar RAGEFEST cools off juat after the 16min mark but Cotter refuses to let the momentum fade and continues his all-out assault on the toms. Peter makes the switch to piano as Rick throws wah-delay riffs around and things explode through another phenomenal peak. Instead of a quick segue, the band then opts for a few minutes of gorgeous major-key play that acts as a prelude to a fantastic "This Old Sea."

This first “Sea” of ‘25 jettisons the tender vocal reprise that had come to characterize some of ‘24’s finest voyages. The band steers toward the rolling, tempestuous format of past “Seas,” with Rick sprinkling southern rock-tinged runs over Cotter’s crashing waves. Calmer waters welcome a brief but gorgeous buoyant theme that signals landfall via a patient and perfect segue -> to "Creatures."

A "Hot Tea" encore for a Friday rager must be your average dance party...right? This absolutely unhinged version comes complete with Cotter and Trevor solo breaks before diving headlong into Westville "Rockdale" territory for several minutes of sustained dissonance. Just when you think it's time to rip back into the ending, the band finds a new vein of inspiration and continues to pour tension over everything. An all-timer performance.

Repurposing the closing note of "Give It Time" as the first note of a surprise standalone "(dawn)", this unfinished version launches into a freeform jam at the mid-point (similarly to the jammed "SOS" the previous weekend in Milwaukee). Cotter keeps a propulsive gallop running underneath a pensive Allmans-y lead from Rick until a bluesy deconstruction leads into "Echo of a Rose".

This incredibly efficient "Echo" wastes no time moving into the first of several themes explored during a brief but satisfying 12 minutes. Lightning fast and telepathic, the band bobs and weaves under some rare flat-picking from Rick. A rollicking cowbell-infused jam and a spacy meltdown transitioning into "Jive II" round out this quality-over-quantity jam. Don't skip this one!
Another worthy entry into the saga of huge, peaky "Big Modern!" jams. Closes out this first set in style via some extra turns around the heavy ending.
The younger sibling of 11/8/24. Peter summons a sampled ocean wave (no, seriously) and the band builds a linear-yet-exciting jam from nothing to an extended peak that Rick just won't let go.

After an unremarkable first half to this relatively short 14-minute "Pancakes," the bottom half of the stack is downright delicious. Rick does that inimitable Rick thing, taking a simple melody and bending it into a euphoric, blissful segment. This shines most brightly at the 11:19 and 13:17 marks, where he runs that melody through cascading, waterfalling runs of pure musical liquid.

The band goes HUGE on the encore for the second night in a row. Gets evil from the get-go with POUNDING Trevor and Cotter as Rick and Peter skip their usual spacey antics in favour of angular play. The tempo amps up and we are thrown headlong into Westville "Rockdale"-style space - edge-of-your-seat madness but with Peter on guitar. Trevor dials in synth effects as it gets crazier, the band setting their sights on the ending but getting there by way of several minutes of punishing darkness and wild sounds.

The "Elmeg" many fans had been waiting for. Breaks out of form into a gorgeous slow build, Peter leading the way at first with some soft textures. Rick takes the lead and gives us the business from there, crafting an epic peak rife with emotion.

Armed with a new palette of 80s-inspired sounds (mostly from Peter), the band strikes into an anthemic, patient build to kick off the year of "Big Modern!." Cools post-peak and eventually works its way through an excellent -> to "Animal."

Debut version immediately asserts itself as a jam vehicle. A very unhurried groove develops with Peter working a hypnotic chord motif, the band loosening things in the final few minutes for a nice layered space with patience and commitment to quieter dynamics. Hints of a bliss build and peak but instead > to "Pancakes."

First version after its Goosemas debut makes a statement on jam potential, reaching out into patient and wide-open space. Hints of "Dragonfly" (another trend of early '26) come in as things get more dense, flying through a great organ-heavy peak before spacing out > to "Wysteria."
Incredible dynamic play early on leads to a bright and bouncy motif, Trevor shining on melodic work. Before too long, the energetic peak fades in favour of "Madalena," sadly abandoning the jam.

jamchart_note: An otherwise run-of-the-mill Goontz version of this song gets augmented by Bogie's sharp tenor sax work.

Quickly getting outside the norm with some tense play, the band hints at some Westville-style jamming. Cotter shines with an unrelenting hold on the tempo, building into a frenzied conclusion with Rick torching the place.

Dogfighting from Rick and Bogie early on resolves into a wide-open bliss landscape. With patience and a commitment to quieter dynamics, the bliss bomb takes shape, sheer beauty only accentuated by the addition of the saxophone.

footnote: Radiohead. With Stuart Bogie on woodwinds.

jamchart_note: The band unlocks a new level of Goontz in this MSG set-closer - dubbed by some the "HYPERGOONTZ." Kind of has to be heard to be believed, but it's pretty nuts.

Moving past an initial Type I peak, Rick and Cotter lock in on some fast-paced minor mode play. Peter makes a rare move to organ for some lead work, turning off the Leslie and stabbing into the jam with some more dissonant elements as the stream of notes from guitar and drums continue, unrelenting. Briefly returning to "Arrow" proper, the band avoids the ending and instead delivers another minute of fast-paced minor play before fading > to "Fish in the Sea."

jamchart_note: It's a "Madhuvan" journey we've heard before - but no less enjoyable. Peter begins by colouring with some ring modulator Rhodes before heading back to guitar. Coalescing around Cotter, the darkness built into a roaring wave before Mitarotonda pulled things into soaring bliss land, the two-guitar peak delivering as it always does.

jamchart_note: A true sunset jam. Rick pulls things out of the typical "AIN" slinky minor key into a gorgeous bliss theme, wringing serious emotion from it as the band follows his lead.

jamchart_note: Cotter leads the way with aggressive cowbell and snare work as Rick and Peter duel it out. Trevor kept things anchored through the peak, juxtaposing the more searching vibe of the guitar and keys against the driving drums.

Tumbling dissonance emerges from the initial peak before Cotter slipped into a fast-paced four-on-the-floor disco groove akin to the 4/18/23 "Rosewood." Building on the back of Peter's clav work, the band explodes back into "EMG" proper while sticking to the dance vibe.

Peter begins the jam with his punchy 80s-inspired synth patch, letting Rick do some digital sauce noodling overtop. The guitarist leads into the darkness and the rhythm section is right with him, both Cotter and Trevor really going ham as Peter cultivates a hypnotic and repeating theme. In a classic Rick move, the churning and heavy peak eventually gives way to a major mode, and he tears through the intense beauty of the second half with incredible melodic contributions from the other three.

Emerges beautifully from a chill groove at the end of a stellar "Thatch." Newly returned to the rig after almost two years, Peter's Nord Lead synth takes centre stage with textures, meshing well with Rick's reverse loops. Great linear build and finish as the band smoothly breaks to sunny territory from the open psychedelia.

Moves past the usual "Modern!" peak and some hints at "Dragonfly" before naturally resolving - spontaneously - into the Goontz. Sticking to an upbeat take rather than the dark "vampire disco" we see more frequently, the band locks in on a repeating three-note phrase and destroys an excellent peak.

show_notes: This show was one set due to a weather delay.

jamchart_note: Some Medeski-like organ play from Peter kicks off the jam, not going full Goontz yet but instead delivering punchy and fast-paced funk. Rick flips on the synth-filter and turns up the heat for several minutes of blistering play. The sequencers eventually enter and the band shifts to Goontz mode, Peter moving to guitar and sawing off huge blocks of sound just in time to match Cotter's big dance drops. Excellent version that goes > to "Rosewood."

Cotter is all in on fluid play, seeming to be everywhere at once while Rick and Peter duel on some inventive, spiralling riffs. Engages second gear into a very Boise-like build, chugging forward into a solid tension/release peak to close the set.

footnote: Otis Day & The Knights. Unfinished. With Secret Agent Man tease from Rick.

jamchart_note: Trevor is aggressive early as Cotter departs into a fluttering beat. Ride cymbal taking centre stage, the band fluidly traverses a few different musical sections as they share ideas, settling into a nice peak and flawless -> to "Butter Rum."

Longest version to date begins with the usual funk, great textural work from Peter leading to a space-out atop Cotter's hi-hat. Trevor gets into some cool tones, meshing with Peter's low synth play to become one big rumble as Rick begins to pick out a gorgeous major-key motif. Reverb-soaked guitar began to lift things up as the band shimmered, soaring higher as Rick smoothly switched between melodic leads and chordal themes. Absolutely phenomenal jam.

"Secret Agent Man" early dissolves into uptempo rock jamming akin to versions of "This Old Sea" and "A Western Sun." A double-time flip from Cotter leads to a big, anthemic peak and the band dangles the "Dragonfly" carrot again - this time the second part.

jamchart_note: The HYPERGOONTZ rears its head again as the band hits a steady disco groove instead of the bouncy major-key jam we've come to expect in recent years. Dominating with heavier play, Peter hops on guitar as the band blows through peaks akin to the Orlando "Creatures" from earlier in the year.

jamchart_note: Peter leads early with marimba piano as Rick lays into steady streams of notes augmented by his harmonized Whammy effect. Flipping to a brighter tone, the band doesn't miss a beat and segues -> to "Electric Avenue," the flow continuing in that song.
-> from "Wysteria." The band picks up right where they left off and continued the peak build, Rick really shining on some explosive soloing.

Pulsating Trevor early on leads to a different kind of jam, where some tumbling dissonance enters the fray. Rick eventually cues a cool progression not unlike the "Modern!" ending, but the band eschews that and instead tears through the moody peak before cooling and -> to "Creatures."

jamchart_note: The follow-up to Toronto and another exemplary showcase of Rick's guitar skills. Evoking some of the greatest bliss peaks in jam history, Trevor really shines on the low-end with wildly creative fills.
Show-opening version gets the treatment as Rick leads the band through an atypical and outside-the-box anthemic peak. Hints of "Loose Ends" throughout.

footnote: With Magic School Bus Theme tease from Peter.

jamchart_note: Opens the SPAC run and debuts Rick's new Lemurian Sceptre guitar in a big way. Immediately heads for dark territory and builds nicely around a theme extremely similar to the Grateful Dead's "Let It Grow."
2026 "Dustin" riffing with a nice little twist. The jam escapes the usual straight-ahead funk build for some floaty minor-key dissonance before returning to form.
Augmented by The Disco Biscuits' lasers, Goose taps into the "HYPERGOONTZ" for some craziness in this version.

With an impending thunderstorm, the band lays waste to SPAC as they develop a thick and churning evil motif. The boil gets more and more forceful as the jam progresses, wrapping the nearly two-hour first set on an insane note.

Escapes typical "Thatch" play thanks to heavy synth pad work from Peter that inspires Cotter. Rick and Trevor poke through the space as they spar, hinting at bliss with a theme similar to the MPP "Arcadia." Imperceptibly infusing the jam with notes of unease, Rick inspires the band to go into a churning, evil mode akin to the 1/30/22 "Wysteria." Trevor continued his incredible play as Peter went in a jazzy direction on piano, the jam getting a lot of added depth as they raged through the darkness.
Marc Brownstein joins the party on bass as Trevor becomes his DJ Marb Menthols alter ego on turntables. Short-lived due to the impending curfew, but a great time nonetheless.

jamchart_note: Very cool dark riffs are uncovered in the first jam, but Rick quickly pulls the ripcord in favour of the first second jam since 8/12/22. Though it's Cotter's first time playing it, he feels right at home in the propulsive groove as the band hits a more dynamic take on the 7/6/21 synth-led style. Rick eventually takes the lead and soars through an incredible and sustained bliss peak.
LONG version that begins with some raging Goontz. In the second half, the band uncovers a new kind of dance jam as Cotter drops an absolutely nasty groove. You will rage, guaranteed.

Patience and commitment to quieter dynamics take over as Rick softly vocalizes along to his melodies. The serene space eventually gives way to a cool ebb-and-flow pattern where the band flips between softer play and rocking power chords based around a triple-hit theme.
The band locks in on one riff and just opens up the hose. Insane amount of energy release in this one.
